survey: A stone park chess table with two stools. Tabletop: a thick square slab with a rounded edge; the chessboard is set into the top face, framed by a stone border, facing up and slightly toward the camera. Table base: one central column that narrows in the middle and widens at both ends; a stepped top block holds the underside of the slab in the middle, and a stepped square plinth stands flat on the grass. The slab overhangs the column evenly, as on real concrete park chess tables. Stools: two round seats on short columns with round bases, one each side of the table, matching in shape and size, each resting on the grass with a shadow. Nothing floats, no parts pass through each other, and there are no loose cables or invented parts. The board's square count could not be checked at full size (the enlarging crop was not approved); if a close count shows more than 8 per side, it would be a minor wrong-count error.
